bull.b: Strong cloud growth, high retention and expanding RPO indicate durable demand for Atlassian’s workflow platform. These metrics support recurring revenue visibility and suggest customers are increasing product usage and commitments over time.

Sustained operating and free cash flow provide financial flexibility to fund product development, artificial intelligence investment and cloud infrastructure. Strong cash conversion despite reported losses demonstrates attractive underlying economics in the subscription model.

Broad enterprise adoption of Rovo and rising platform engagement strengthen Atlassian’s strategic position in team workflows and enterprise automation. The Teamwork Graph and ecosystem can deepen customer dependence and support future cross-sell opportunities.

bear.b: Ongoing GAAP losses limit reported profitability and keep returns on equity negative. Although cash generation is strong, continued accounting losses may constrain financial quality and increase reliance on operating leverage to support long-term shareholder returns.

The lower ARR outlook versus FY26 and reduced margin guide imply that growth may normalize while investment and execution costs remain elevated. This creates a more demanding path to durable profitability despite strong recent operating momentum.

Balance-sheet leverage has improved but remains material relative to equity, while negative ROE reflects continued accounting losses. This reduces financial flexibility compared with a debt-light software peer and could amplify pressure during weaker growth periods.
